pure-announcement.rationale: It is a practitioner guide to a kernel-level observability technique, not a launch or release note, despite closing with a training-course plug.

duplicate.rationale: The nearest concepts are all MCP/agent-security topics; the corpus holds nothing on eBPF, sidecar overhead, or kernel-level telemetry.

unfalsifiable.rationale: The central mechanism claims are reproducible via the included helm/kubectl commands, though side statistics like the uncited '67% CNCF survey' figure and the author's bank anecdotes are not independently checkable.

durability.rationale: The core argument — one kernel-level program per node observes every container, removing per-pod sidecar cost and the SDK instrumentation coverage gap — is an architectural trade-off that outlives the pinned Cilium/Beyla versions and 2026 adoption stats decorating it.

actionability.rationale: It gives a phased migration plan with concrete commands, per-node resource sizing, a kernel-version decision matrix, and named failure modes (PSA conflicts, Pixie OOM on small nodes, CNI cutover drops) a team can act on directly.

atomicity.rationale: The four tools are presented as layers of one coherent thesis — zero-instrumentation observability from the kernel up — which is statable in a single paragraph without the source's framing.
